content.thinking:
I'm planning the file structure carefully before writing anything, thinking through whether to use plain objects with a builder pattern and deciding I need at least one root joint to avoid resolution errors for parts without an assigned bone.

Now I'm sketching out the bookshelf's dimensions and layout: roughly 1.5m wide, 1.85m tall with a crown and pinnacles, 0.4m deep, with three shelf bays and side posts, then thinking through helper functions for boxes and how to apply cel-shaded paints versus flat colors to stay within the palette limit.

For texture budget, I'm using a larger 2048 paint sheet for crisper cel edges, saving flat colors for small gold trims and reserving painted cel textures for wood grain and book covers, then planning a book-building helper that constructs standing books with front/back covers, page blocks, and spine details.

For the book geometry, I'm working out cover slabs on each side with a spine slab facing forward and a pages box inset to peek out as cream between the covers at top, plus gold band decorations across the spine.

For spine decoration, I'm planning small gold emblem textures (star, crescent, diamond) rendered on thin planes positioned just in front of each spine. With roughly 8 parts per book across 24 books, that's about 192 parts total, which stays well under the budget, and I'm sketching out the overall shelf layout from the viewer's perspective.

Working through the coordinate convention, screen-right maps directly to +X, so I can place objects using screen coordinates without inversion. Then I'm laying out each bay from the reference image: top bay has standing colored books with an orb, scrolls, and a candle; middle bay has more books, a stacked pair with a clasp, a teal orb on a tripod, candles, and an armillary sphere; bottom bay continues with scrolls and books.

Now I'm defining the precise vertical frame for the shelf structure -- plinth height, board thicknesses, and the top/bottom y-values for each of the three bays, plus the crown section above with an arched outline and crescent decal, and the post positions at x=±0.7.

Working out post dimensions next -- centered width, full height with a cap block and gold pyramid pinnacle on top, giving an overall tall wizard bookshelf shape. I'm placing the back panel as a thin dark wood box with vertical plank grain, and defining the depth and placement of the side posts and front pilasters, now adding gold trim details to the posts.

Still refining decorative elements...

Still writing SVG code...

Now I'm mapping out the crown's outline points relative to its anchor position, forming a gentle scalloped silhouette with smoothing applied so the peaks and curves round off naturally rather than appearing sharp.

I'm adding small pinnacle blocks on either side of the crown for detail, then setting up the wood paint definitions using cel-shaded grain textures with vertical and horizontal axis variants for different parts of the structure.

Now I'm defining the book cover colors as flat cel-shaded paints—red, blue, green, purple, teal—plus a mottled leather texture variant.

I'll just use flat gold for simplicity since the renderer handles lighting anyway. Now I'm sketching helper functions like `box()` that wraps geometry creation with position, color, and bone attachment, so rigid parts placed at a given point stay correctly anchored to the root bone.

For painted parts I should avoid sharing geometry objects across instances since paint bakes into colors/UVs, so I'll just create fresh geometry each time since it's cheap. For books, I'm designing a builder function that places boxes upright with optional decorations and tilt, though true leaning requires composing transforms manually since parts only support per-part rotation, so I'm working out a placer using a transform matrix for composite positioning.

I'm defining a frame abstraction with position and quaternion so I can place boxes and planes in a local coordinate system that gets rotated into world space, letting decals on book spines face the right direction without baking extra rotations into the geometry itself.

That makes sense since spine decals face forward locally. Now I'm sketching gold-colored SVG shapes for decorations: a four-point star path, an eight-point starburst made from two overlapped stars, and a crescent moon using circle subtraction.

Still writing SVG code...

I'm also designing a diamond shape with an inner line, a cross-shaped clasp made from a rectangle and circle, and figuring out how to size these decorations relative to the spine face. Now I'm planning where these decorative bands should sit along each book's spine.

I'm working out book dimensions—thickness around 0.045-0.07, height 0.24-0.34—and figuring out how deep books sit on the shelf so they appear flush near the front like the reference image, settling on a z-center around 0.06 with depth 0.24.

Now I'm defining the book-building function itself: left and right cover boxes with thin thickness, a spine box along the back, and cream-colored pages set slightly shorter than the covers so the covers protrude a bit above, below, and at the edges for a realistic look.

I'm considering adding optional gold corner brackets for certain books and maybe a ribbon bookmark or tassel for clasp-style covers, though keeping these lightweight additions optional rather than universal. Now I'm tallying up the total part count per book, factoring in covers, spine, pages, and bands.

Then I need to handle books lying flat in stacks rather than standing upright, which means figuring out how to orient a book horizontally—deciding where the spine, fore-edge, and pages face relative to the stack so it matches the reference image's layout.

Still computing book geometry...

For the orbs, I'm thinking about glossy purple/teal spheres for the wizard stands — maybe a glowing flat-colored sphere layered with a swirled texture, since a radial gradient won't wrap cleanly onto sphere UVs, so I'll try combining an inner glowing sphere with an outer highlight layer.

Generating wavy band texture...

Adding tripod stand geometry and candle holder lathe profiles...

Still building the flame and candle details...

Now I'm designing the scrolls as rolled parchment cylinders with spiral end caps, cream-colored paper, darker edge discs, and wrapped ribbons with a gold wax seal, arranged in a small stack.

Working out the pyramid arrangement for three scrolls: two sit side by side at the bottom, touching, with the third resting centered on top using trigonometry to find the correct vertical offset so they stack naturally.

For the leaning scroll bundle, I'm designing a reusable scroll function with rotation parameters so each piece can tilt at a slight angle and stand upright, built from a cylindrical body plus rim discs at the ends.

Still refining scroll geometry...

Adding a thin gold rod tail hanging from the seal for the scroll stack, then designing the armillary sphere for the shelf -- gold rings in different orientations plus an inner globe, tilted 23° on a stand with a base and axis rod.

For bay 3, I'm placing a cradled cream sphere nestled inside gold rings, then shaping a glowing blue potion bottle with a lathe profile and a gold neck collar with cork.

Now I'm adding small accents like a gold medallion pendant with a star and a tiny highlight sphere, plus hanging ornaments from the posts: a gold crescent moon with chain and blue crystal on the left post, and a lantern with purple tassel on the right, using rod geometry for the chains and double-sided card planes for the crescent texture.

Designing the hanging crescent SVG with a star and crystal...

Still building the lantern...

Then I'm planning the floor items: a stack of two tilted books in blue and red, plus a scroll with a seal and a hanging gold charm, positioned toward the front-left.

Working out post bases and a shaped apron board between them with an arched outline, extruded for thickness.

Still plotting apron outline coordinates...

I'm adding a dark plinth box beneath the apron to make contact with the floor at y=0, sizing and positioning it so it overlaps slightly behind the apron's front face without visible gaps.

Now designing the vertical posts: raised front pilaster panels in a darker wood tone, decorative gold diamond decals partway up, and a wider collar block capping the top of each post with gold banding details.

Continuing with the cap — adding another gold collar, a small pedestal block, and a four-sided pyramid cone on top to finish the post's ornamental tip.

For the pinnacle itself, I'll build an octahedron-style diamond shape using two four-sided cones joined base-to-base, one upright and one inverted, both painted gold.

Now I'm reconsidering the crown's top board — it should sit between the posts around y=1.46–1.5, with a thicker beveled top rail added above the painted wood cap for a more accurate profile.

I'm recalculating shelf heights to keep clear bay spacing consistent at roughly .38–.40 each, adjusting shelf tops to .20, .62, and 1.04 with the underside of the top board at 1.44, and defining each shelf board as a thin .04-thick box positioned just below its listed top height.

Now I'm adding a lighter-colored front edge rim to each shelf for a subtle highlight, and placing a thin back panel box spanning the shelf unit's width and height set slightly behind the shelves.

I'm also drawing vertical plank lines on the back panel, seven dark thin strips evenly spaced, to give it a wooden board texture. I'll skip adding gold star appliqués on the back for now and move to laying out books within each bay, naming the three bay heights low, mid, and top so I can position book objects within their interior bounds.

For the top bay, I'm placing red, blue, and green books side by side starting from the left edge, carefully spacing their centers so each book's width doesn't overlap its neighbor, leaving small gaps between them. I'm also planning to add a small gold bookend shape, like an L-shaped gilded plate, at the far left of this row to match the ornate reference style.

Continuing outward, I'll add a crescent-shaped bookend after the green book, then place a decorative orb on a short stand further right, followed by a stack of scrolls, a candle in its holder, and another small post, filling out the shelf with varied object heights and silhouettes. Now I'm shifting to plan out the middle bay's layout.

Adding the small candle holder and checking the tripod orb's placement relative to the stacked books, then moving to the low bay where I'm positioning a leaning bundle of three upright scrolls with varying roll angles.

Next I'm placing the colored books (green, blue, red) along the bay, then a potion bottle nearby. I'm also arranging a flat stack of colored boxes (purple, green, red) centered right, plus an armillary globe with rings to the right, staggering the stack slightly for visual variety.

Checking the stack height clears the top shelf fine. Then I'm tallying up the total object count across all the standing books, flat stacks, orbs, candles, scrolls, armillary spheres, potions, frame, and decor pieces to estimate roughly 450 parts total, keeping triangle counts low by limiting torus segments.

Setting up wood coloring on box geometry...

Working out the typing for fill colors as string or Paint, and being careful with imports since I can't run a typechecker — sticking to minimal, necessary imports like THREE, createBuilder, frame helpers, and toon/glow kit utilities while skipping anything unused like rng or catmull.

Setting up the module structure now: importing grain, mix, and mottle for paint effects, svg for texture, and the cel/glow kit helpers, then defining meta info and a color palette with gold tones for the design.

Adding more palette colors...

I'm caching leather textures by building a mottled surface darkened from the base color and running it through the toon shading helper, memoizing results per color key so repeated calls don't recompute.

Given the module-level caching concerns, I'm deciding to move everything—paints and textures alike—inside the build() function as closures so nothing leaks state across builds. Defining more star-shaped texture patterns...

Working out the crescent moon shape, layering two overlapping arcs to carve out the lit portion with the right orientation...

Still calculating arc radii...

Checking sweep flag direction: sweep=1 moving clockwise from bottom through left to top matches the small bulge, and the large arc from top to bottom with sweep=0 passes counterclockwise through left with center positioned left of the chord.

Now I'm sketching the texture icons: a diamond shape with nested gold and parchment layers, a clasp texture using rectangles and circles for a buckle look, and a spiral texture using a circular parchment crop with a spiral path.

Writing orb textures...

Then I'm designing a flame icon with layered teardrop paths—an outer orange flame, a yellow inner flame, and a smaller white-hot core—to give it depth.

For the crescent hanging moon, I'm scaling the moon path and positioning it with a chain line rendered as a thick gold stroke, following the reference of a moon hanging from a post with a star below and a crystal to the side.

Below that I'm adding a small blue hexagon crystal with a connecting link line, then moving to the apron design—a gold arc shape with a star centered near the top, working out the proportions in the smaller viewBox.

Now I'm setting up the crown texture, drawing a swoosh curve that follows the crown's silhouette inset from the edge.

I'm checking whether my decorative swoosh curve roughly tracks the crown's outline coordinates, converting between meters and pixels to see how far it deviates—looks like it sits inset by a small margin, which works fine for a stylized decorative element.

Now I need to size the crown's plane geometry. Since the outline shape spans wider than my initial rectangle estimate, I should widen the plane dimensions to properly contain the texture and recalculate its z-depth relative to the medallion's front face.

Setting up the build function now...

Adding helper functions for positioning...

Adding a decal helper for textured planes, setting up a world-frame origin, and starting a book-building function that constructs leather-bound covers with spine and corner geometry...

Checking the pages' z-position and depth math against the spine so they sit properly inset within the cover, and considering whether to add faint page-line texture or skip that detail for simplicity.

Now I'm placing decorative gold bands on the spine at specific height ratios, verifying how their depth and position align relative to the spine's front face so they sit flush rather than floating.

I'm also planning the emblem decals on the cover — a main one centered at mid-height plus smaller star and diamond accents near the quarter marks, though I'm wary of cluttering thinner book spines with too many decorations.

Now I'm sketching a flat-book builder function: thin top and bottom boards, a front cover plate, and an inner page block sized to fit inside the covers with small margins.

Adding gold emblem decals and decorative stars at measured positions, deciding to skip corner caps for lying books, then moving to the scroll function.

I'm building a cylindrical scroll shape rotated so its axis runs along x, with a parchment texture using grain-based paint for roll lines, and rims at both ends.

Adding seal and ribbon details...

Now I'm sketching the orb helper function, which wraps a glowing sphere using the given texture and tints it white, plus small specular highlight spheres positioned for a sense of light reflection.

Simplifying rotation and scale of those highlight dots, then moving on to building the crescent cradle stand using layered gold cylinders.

Writing crescent torus geometry...

For the tripod mid-bay I'm placing a horizontal ring and three support rods down to feet, then working out the orb's resting height on the ring using the geometry of a sphere sitting in a torus — radius .07 orb on a .06 ring puts its center around y=.121. Small foot spheres finish the tripod, then I'm moving on to the candle.

I'm sketching the candle holder as a lathed profile, shaping it with a tapered base, flared lip, and a decorative notch, scaled by a "big" flag for larger vs smaller candles, with a star decal planned for the front face.

Still writing geometry...

Writing armillary sphere geometry...

Adding axis rod, orbiting moon planet on the equator ring, and a connecting stand rod from the base to the ring's underside...

Now I'm shaping a glowing potion using a lathe profile with defined outline points for the vessel's silhouette.

Still placing gold trim and glow details...

I'm also considering small shelf accessories like a quill and inkwell, but deciding to skip them in favor of simpler details like a hanging tassel near the spine.

Now I'm defining the bedpost frame geometry—shaft dimensions, front panel colors with grain texture, and the foot block positioning.

Still writing frame coordinates...

Still placing finial geometry...

Still placing hardware...

Still laying out lantern geometry...

Still shaping the tassel skirt...

For the lantern, I'm adding a small star decal plate to the glass sides, tinted gold against the orange glow — not luminous itself but readable enough. Now moving on to extruding the crown shape.

Defining crown outline points...

I'll skip the outer rim gold line since the decal already covers it. Checking z-depth placement, the crown at z=-0.1 sits properly in front of the back board, and I'm now working out the top board's width dimensions.

Still placing trim pieces...

Working out the apron's wavy outline shape, adjusting y-coordinates so it sits flush with the shelf board and plinth without clashing.

I'm positioning the apron decal plane and checking that its texture coordinates align with the apron's drawn curve edges — verifying the bottom and side points match up in world space so the arc doesn't appear misaligned with the apron outline.

Now I'm moving on to planning the floor objects, figuring out placement for the post foot blocks and a nearby floor stack, positioning them at specific x and z coordinates near the front bottom of the scene.

Still working out charm geometry...

I'll drop the floor charm idea and stick with ribbon tails instead. For the leaning scroll bundle in the low bay, I'm positioning three upright scrolls with a slight roll offset for lean, anchoring their base position to the shelf height.

Working out each scroll's center y-coordinate based on its length and lean angle, so they rest against the wall diagonally as shown in the reference, touching each other naturally.

I'm checking the third scroll's top edge against the nearby book slightly overlaps, so I'm nudging the book positions for green, blue, and red to clear spacing, then verifying the potion, stack, and armillary sphere placements all fit within their bounds without collisions.

Now I'm working through the mid-bay layout, placing the armillary sphere, blue and purple books, red book, central stack, tripod orb, and candles, adjusting x-coordinates to avoid overlaps between the tripod's feet and the candle holders.

For the top bay, I'm positioning the bookend plate, red/blue/green books, the crescent bookend, and the orb cradle, checking each item's width against its neighbors to keep gaps consistent and avoid clipping.

Then I'm laying out the right side: the scroll stack and orb edge, the candle holder, and noticing a gap between the scroll and candle, so I'll fill it with a small inkwell and quill — a dark cylinder with a gold cap plus a tilted rod and extruded feather vane in cream and blue-white.

Picking a y-direction tilted toward the viewer so it's perpendicular to x, then adding a thin rod running from the quill's base to tip in gold/cream. Now I'm working out the low bay book stack, positioning red, green, and purple books with slight yaw rotations and staggered heights so the purple top book stays safely under the shelf limit.

Still writing book positions...

Now I'm working out the top-bay scroll stack positioning, placing scrolls along the x-axis with slight yaw variation and staggered row offsets, assigning alternating red and purple ribbon colors to each stack, and figuring out which scrolls should show a visible seal on their front face.

I'm also designing the gold gear bookends — placing plates with cylindrical cog shapes and hubs rotated along the x-axis, plus a crescent-shaped bookend plate positioned further along.

I'm deciding to skip extra decorative touches like dust-mote cards, glow sparkles, and radial halos around the orb to keep things simpler, and noting the overall flat color palette being used across the scene.

Then I tally the texture atlas, counting around twelve distinct textures for elements like stars, moons, diamonds, clasps, flames, and crowns, each getting its own tile.

Writing orb texture generator...

Checking the sine wave connects smoothly at both edges since it's periodic, then starting on a spiral texture using polar coordinates with increasing radius for a circular pattern.

Now I'm building the hanging crystal shape as an SVG with a thick stroke outline and gradient fill...

Checking the chain-moon connection point and verifying the crescent moon's curve aligns properly with the scaled transform coordinates.

For plane dimensions and stroke width conversion to physical units — now setting up the flame card frames using the frame utility, sizing them with cross and flow parameters before applying a glow effect of 1.4.

Checking the lathe function's option fields (at, axis, segments, color, bone) and the rod signature taking two points, radius, color, and options with bone attachment. Verifying glow works correctly across lathe parts, array results from cards, and orb outputs, confirming the Part type's mesh getter matches the Glowing interface requirements.

Noting that painted parts break glow (so I need flat or textured ones only), and confirming texture parts use unique materials per texture so cloning for glow stays safe. I'm mapping out the option types for part placement (position, quaternion, bone, scale as number or vector) and reminding myself to avoid unused variable declarations as I write out the full implementation.

Now I'm defining several wood color variants with grain textures at different axes and seeds for variety, then I'll move on to writing a leather material function.

Next I'm picking flat cover colors for the books—red, blue, green, purple, teal—and setting up a helper function to place books in a shelf bay with consistent depth and positioning.

Still placing bay books...

Still positioning candle drips and flames...

For the gear and hub, I'm skipping the detailed teeth ring and keeping things simple with cylinders for the gear body and hub. I need to double-check the armillary sphere orientation and orb highlight sizing, then watch for naming clashes like the flatBook parameter conflicting with D, switching to "dp" instead. For the scroll ribbon, I'm using a torus rotated so its plane aligns properly with the x-axis.

Now I'm placing tripod rods in a triangular arrangement around the sphere, computing ring and foot points at 120-degree intervals, adding small foot spheres, and closing it off with a horizontal torus ring. I'm also making sure all frames use identity rotation and double-checking TypeScript typing for the book function parameters, plus confirming the floor scroll's orientation along the x-axis and avoiding naming collisions with the decal helper.

Writing SVG star path...
